output.murderer: Dr Casimir Vauthier, the family physician
output.reasoning: Anchors: the hall clock struck ten when the regulator, which agreed with the bell, showed 9:48. So the hall strike runs 12 minutes early, and it struck eleven at true 22:48. Rosa's kitchen clock showed 11:13 at that strike, so it runs 25 minutes fast. (Monnier had tampered with it, which is why Rosa's "15 minutes fast" is wrong.) Lina's arrival at 22:47 by that clock is true 22:22, which fits with her leaving the atelier at 22:20. The piano ran from kitchen 22:58 to 23:11, which is true 22:33 to 22:46. So the doctor was out of the salon from about 22:33 to 22:46. Girard saw the piano start at his 10:29, so his watch is 4 minutes slow. His "faint quick bells" at 10:34 are therefore true 22:38. Félix's watch was 20 minutes slow at nine. His thump and repeater at 10:18 are also true 22:38 if the offset held. The 22:05 stop on the regulator is a false setting by the murderer. Rosa and Lina were together in the kitchen, Odile was at the piano, Girard was in the street and Félix was in the library. The only person free and able to reach the atelier at 22:38 is the doctor. He is also the one who says he tampered with his watch ("never managed to leave it alone"). He gave 10:45 for his departure by his watch, which does not fit the true 22:33 he left the room.
